summary: Checks whether a value is **not** empty.
description: `nonEmpty(value)` is the same test as `!isEmpty(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Emptiness is read per kind: `null` and `undefined`, a string with nothing but whitespace, an array, `Set` or `Map` with no entries, an object with no own keys. `0` and `false` are values, not emptiness.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not empty; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonEmpty(0); // => true
nonEmpty(false); // => true
nonEmpty("a"); // => true
nonEmpty([0]); // => true
nonEmpty(null); // => false
nonEmpty(""); // => false
nonEmpty("   "); // => false
nonEmpty([]); // => false
nonEmpty({}); // => false
nonEmpty(new Map()); // => false
```
